newsitem.title: UK: Balloon heart therapy said to reduce chest pain.
newsitem.headline: Balloon heart therapy said to reduce chest pain.

text.p: Patients with heart disease experience less chest pain from treatment with a mechanical procedure involving tiny balloons than from drugs, according to a study published in the British medical journal The Lancet on Friday.
The study, citing data collected midway through a five-year clinical trial, showed that widening narrowed arteries with tiny balloons improved exercise tolerance as well as reducing chest pain.
Tne procedure is known as percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA).
The trial involved 1,018 patients recruited from 20 cardiology centres in Britain and Ireland.
About half the patients were randomly allocated PTCA and the other half were assigned treatment with drugs.
At the midpoint, the PTCA group had a significantly greater risk of death. However, the absolute risk was low in both groups, the authors wrote.
The authors concluded that the benefits of PTCA over drugs were significant for patients with the severest chest pain and a low tolerance for exercise.

"We demonstrated that PTCA improves symptoms (angina and breathlessness), reduces the requirement for anti-anginal medication, and improves exercise tolerance compared with medical therapy," they said.
